title: Moral AI and the Erosion of Its Own Demand
abstract: arXiv:2611.25213v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study the evolution of human preference frequencies and AI adoption when individuals can choose between a moral AI that rules out defection and an unconstrained AI that preserves discretion. By allowing users to commit to cooperation, moral AI can sustain cooperation even when cooperative preferences are too scarce to do so on their own. But this success has a cost. By turning otherwise dormant cooperative preferences into committed behavior, moral AI exposes its users to exploitation by selfish individuals, causing the population share of conditional cooperators to decline under evolutionary selection. As conditional cooperators become less prevalent, equilibrium adoption eventually converges to zero. Moral AI can therefore be self-liquidating. For initial shares between the moral-AI adoption cutoff and the threshold for cooperation without AI, moral AI generates cooperation while lowering the limiting share of conditional cooperator

translated_title: 道德AI及其自身需求的侵蚀
translated_abstract: 我们研究了当个体可以在排除背叛行为的道德AI与保留自主决定权的无约束AI之间进行选择时，人类偏好频率的演化与AI的采用动态。通过让用户承诺合作，即使合作性偏好稀少到无法自发维持合作，道德AI也能够维持合作。但这种成功是有代价的：道德AI将原本处于休眠状态的合作性偏好转化为承诺性行为，从而使其用户暴露于自私个体的剥削之下，导致条件合作者在演化选择下的种群份额不断下降。随着条件合作者变得越来越稀少，均衡采用率最终收敛于零。因此，道德AI可能是自我消解的。对于初始份额介于道德AI采用临界点与无AI合作阈值之间的情形，道德AI虽然能够促成合作，但同时会降低条件合作者的极限份额。
tldr: 道德AI虽能通过承诺机制维持合作，但其成功反而使条件合作者在演化选择中逐渐减少，最终导致自身采用率收敛为零，呈现出“自我消解”的特性。
en_tdlr: Moral AI can sustain cooperation by committing users to cooperate, but its success erodes the population share of conditional cooperators under evolutionary selection, ultimately driving its own adoption to zero—making moral AI self-liquidating.
